title: OmniVia Chat Runtime Contract v1 - W2-W4 command surface
description: Freezes the initial Chat command names (technical delivery specification §10) as a closed registry and gives each a bounded wire shape, without turning the Chat family into an Application Contract v1/v2-style exhaustive operation catalogue. `CommitMessageAmendment` is deliberately not repeated here: it closes CGAP-042-006 with its own dedicated request/result pair in amendment.schema.json. Commands that trigger App, Workflow, Agent, Tool or Artifact execution (`InvokeTool`, `InvokeApp`, `StartWorkflow`, `StartAgentRun`, `ReviseArtifact`, `PlaceArtifactVersion`) carry only a `TargetReference` and a bounded opaque `input`; Chat originates no operation semantics for those owning authorities (`generation.schema.json` WorkKind/WorkProjection). Every command declares idempotency by `commandId` (REF042-INV-015, REF042-INV-016) and every result distinguishes a fresh commit from an idempotent replay.

ChatCommandName.title: ChatCommandName
ChatCommandName.description: The closed v1 initial Chat command registry (technical delivery specification §10). Fail closed on an unknown name.

CommandResultEnvelope.title: CommandResultEnvelope
CommandResultEnvelope.description: The one stable command-result envelope frozen by the accepted technical delivery specification §10: every Chat command result is reportable through this closed shape regardless of its own richer, typed result record (`CommandAck`, `MessageSubmittedResult`, etc., which MAY be carried by reference in `resultRef`). `status` is closed to `accepted | completed | rejected | conflict`. Deterministic error/version rule: `error` is required for `rejected`; `error` and `currentVersion` are both optional for `conflict`, so a caller may see a stable error explaining the conflict, a `currentVersion` to re-read and retry, both, or neither; `error` is forbidden for `accepted` and `completed`. `error.code` is a value from the frozen, stable, shared `ErrorCode` registry (`common.schema.json#/$defs/ErrorCode`), never an arbitrary string, and `error.message` is bounded and display-safe, never a raw exception. `currentVersion` is generic command-conflict resource-version context, not itself a `ConversationViewState` optimistic-concurrency token: it uses the generic `ResourceVersion` type because the resource in conflict is not always a view-state row.

resultRef.description: Optional opaque reference to this command's own typed result record, when one exists.

CommandAck.title: CommandAck
CommandAck.description: The shared result shape for a command whose only durable effect is a state transition already fully described elsewhere (for example `RenameConversation`, `ArchiveConversation`, `DeleteConversation`, `SelectConversationPath`, `SetDefaultConversationPath`, `DiscardDraft`, `CancelQueuedSubmission`, `ReorderQueuedSubmission`, `RemoveStagedAttachment`, `StopGeneration`).

CreateScopedConversationRequest.title: CreateScopedConversationRequest
CreateScopedConversationRequest.description: Creates a Conversation pre-scoped to a Chat command target (technical delivery specification §10), for example a Conversation opened from within an App or Workflow context.

DeleteConversationRequest.title: DeleteConversationRequest
DeleteConversationRequest.description: Realised as tombstone-under-policy, never a physical purge of a shared ancestor (REF-042 §25.1, §25.3).

SubmitMessageRequest.title: SubmitMessageRequest
SubmitMessageRequest.description: Normal continuation on the actor's resolved active branch (REF-042 §9.2, §15.4). Carries expected branch head to prevent accidental append to a stale head (REF-042 §15.4, §21.4). The expected-head group -- `branchId`, `expectedHeadMessageId`, `expectedHeadVersion` -- is required all-or-none. All three together is the continuation this command has always been. All three absent is the first send into a Conversation that has no branch yet: REF-042 §9.1 gives a new Conversation no branch until its first committed user Message, so there is no head for the caller to state and a synthetic one would be a fabricated expectation rather than a stale-head check. Any partial group is refused: a caller that states one of the three has a view of a head, and the two it left out are exactly the halves that would go unchecked.

StopGenerationRequest.title: StopGenerationRequest
StopGenerationRequest.description: Cancellation changes Generation Job state; it does not remove committed Messages (REF-042 §17.6).

RetryGenerationRequest.title: RetryGenerationRequest
RetryGenerationRequest.description: Creates a new Generation Attempt under the same Job (REF-042 §17.4). Distinct from `RegenerateResponse`, which creates a new sibling assistant Message on a new branch (ADR-022 §4.14).

ProviderRouteBinding.title: ProviderRouteBinding
ProviderRouteBinding.description: The host-authorized Provider route a Generation Job executes on, snapshotted durably onto the job (and onto a queued submission) when it is created, so queued work, retries, continuations and crash recovery keep the route chosen for that job while later jobs may use a different one. Execution authority supplied by the trusted host, never renderer display state: it is not projected into any snapshot or query result. Both members are required; a partial route is refused.

RegenerateResponseRequest.title: RegenerateResponseRequest
RegenerateResponseRequest.description: Creates a sibling assistant Message under the same user parent with a `regeneration` derivation relation (ADR-022 §4.14, REF-042 §9.4). The original assistant Message and its descendants remain (REF-042 §9.4).

SelectConversationPathRequest.title: SelectConversationPathRequest
SelectConversationPathRequest.description: REF-042 §15.3 `SelectConversationBranch`. Updates view state only; never increments graph revision (REF042-RULE-009).

SetDefaultConversationPathRequest.title: SetDefaultConversationPathRequest
SetDefaultConversationPathRequest.description: Sets `Conversation.defaultBranchId` (REF-042 §7.1, §4.18). Not organisational truth and does not invalidate alternatives.

StageAttachmentRequest.title: StageAttachmentRequest
StageAttachmentRequest.description: Stages an already-uploaded File Reference for composition. Never accepts raw bytes on this wire boundary.

ReviewDecisionRequest.title: ReviewDecisionRequest
ReviewDecisionRequest.description: C8. Decides one open Review wait -- `approved` or `denied`, once, for the action the reviewer was shown. Mirrors `service/chat_tool_review.decide_tool_review` argument for argument; a field invented here is a field that library rejects at runtime. `targetActionDigest` and `targetResourceRevision` echo what the reviewer saw and are stated even when null, because a decision that cannot say what it was shown is not a reviewable one. `currentResourceRevision`, where the caller knows it, refuses a Review of a resource that has moved since. Deliberately NO `conversationId`: the wait row names its own conversation, and a second statement of it would admit a disagreement nobody could resolve.

waitId.description: The open wait this decision answers.

expectedRequestVersion.description: The wait request version the reviewer acted on. A decision against a superseded version is refused, never applied.

targetActionDigest.description: The action digest the reviewer was shown, or null where the wait carries none. Bounds are migration 0071's own CHECK: `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex, length exactly 71.

targetResourceRevision.description: The resource revision the reviewer was shown, or null. Non-negative, per 0071's CHECK.

currentResourceRevision.description: Optional. The caller's current revision, which refuses a Review of a resource that has moved since it was shown.

auditRef.description: Optional caller-supplied audit reference, stored verbatim.

SubmitHumanInputRequest.title: SubmitHumanInputRequest
SubmitHumanInputRequest.description: C8. Answers one open human-input wait. Mirrors `service/chat_tool_review.submit_human_input` argument for argument. Only a digest and the byte length of `answer` become durable -- the answer itself is never persisted -- so this command is the one place its content exists at all. The wire closes the answer's outer envelope to the same maximum eight stable field IDs and scalar value kinds a `HumanInputPrompt` can define; Core then validates the exact keys, required fields, types, options and text lengths against the authoritative prompt stored on the wait. `MAX_ANSWER_BYTES` still caps canonical UTF-8 at 16384 bytes, and the wait's own `prompt.maxAnswerBytes` may bound it further and defaults to 4096.

waitId.description: The open wait this answer closes.

answer.description: The person's bounded answer, keyed by the authoritative prompt's stable field IDs. Values are only the scalar kinds its closed field types admit; Core validates the object against that exact prompt before settlement, and only its digest and byte length become durable.

CreateConversationShareRequest.title: CreateConversationShareRequest
CreateConversationShareRequest.description: REF-042 §18.1-§18.2. Shares the selected branch snapshot by default; sharing all branches requires an explicit, separately permission-checked scope.

ExportConversationRequest.title: ExportConversationRequest
ExportConversationRequest.description: REF-042 §18.3. `branchIds` names one branch for `selected_branch_snapshot` and one or more for `all_accessible_branches_snapshot`.

SubmitSteeringInputRequest.title: SubmitSteeringInputRequest
SubmitSteeringInputRequest.description: Submits one text-only Direction (C6) to a running Generation Job. Closed and deliberately narrow: it names the target Job and the Job `version` the caller observed (`expectedGenerationVersion`, a real control token), states that it expects the Job to be exactly `running` and asks for exactly the `earliest_safe` boundary, and carries only bounded authored `editableParts` as closed, text-only `DirectionTextPart`s (canonical authored text; no image, URL or arbitrary payload key). `attachmentReferences` and `contextReferences` are required but may only be empty in C6: there is no reference or target seam on this command. `supersedesDirectionId` is the one optional seam, naming an earlier Direction this one replaces. `commandId` is the sole idempotency key; the Direction identity is server-issued and never stated here.

editableParts.description: The authored Direction content: closed, text-only `DirectionTextPart`s. Bounded to fit the Direction's durable row: at most 16 parts of at most 4000 Unicode code points each, and the canonical JSON object `{"editableParts": [...]}` stored as the Direction's content -- keys sorted, compact separators, non-ASCII emitted as itself, as `to_canonical_json` serializes it -- is at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. JSON Schema cannot compare an aggregate UTF-8 byte length, so that limit is normative contract metadata enforced by the package codec (`validate_direction_content`; `DIRECTION_CONTENT_MAX_UTF8_BYTES`), not by this keyword set.

DirectionSubmittedResult.title: DirectionSubmittedResult
DirectionSubmittedResult.description: The typed result of `SubmitSteeringInput` (C6). Identity and state only: a successful submit durably creates the Direction `pending` (it is never applied, superseded, rejected or cancelled by the act of submitting), so `state` is exactly `pending`; a Direction that is already terminal is read back through the `Direction` projection, not through this result. It never echoes the authored content, which is read back through the actor-scoped `Direction` projection.

ReferencedWorkCommandRequest.title: ReferencedWorkCommandRequest
ReferencedWorkCommandRequest.description: The shared shape for `RespondToWorkRequest`, `InvokeTool`, `InvokeApp`, `StartWorkflow`, `StartAgentRun`, `ReviseArtifact` and `PlaceArtifactVersion`. `SubmitSteeringInput` is deliberately not part of this shape: it steers Chat's own running Generation Job and has its own closed `SubmitSteeringInputRequest`. Every one of these commands triggers or responds to execution owned entirely by another authority (App, Workflow, Agent, Tool or Artifact ownership); Chat contributes only the triggering Message context, a `TargetReference` and a bounded opaque `input`, and never originates operation semantics for the referenced authority (freeze §7).
